Names and codes

Source: vignettes/names-and-codes.Rmd
names-and-codes.Rmd

A place can have several spellings. Khovsgol, Khuvsgul, Khövsgöl and Хөвсгөл refer to the same aimag. mongolmaps connects these names to one place code. Use codes when joining data; use names for labels.

library(mongolmaps)

Find a place code

mn_match() returns a P-code by default. You can ask for another column, such as name_mn or nso_code, with to.

mn_match(c("Khuvsgul", "Hovsgol", "Khövsgöl", "Хөвсгөл", "MN-041", "267"))
#> [1] "MN67" "MN67" "MN67" "MN67" "MN67" "MN67"
mn_match(c("MN84", "MN8401"), to = "name_mn")
#> [1] "Ховд"      "Жаргалант"

Choose a code system

  • pcode: a unique code across the package’s administrative levels.
  • nso_code: the code used in National Statistics Office tables.
  • iso_code: ISO 3166-2 for aimags and Ulaanbaatar; not available at every level.

This table comes from the package’s crosswalk rather than a hand-written list. Store codes as text to preserve their formatting.

examples <- mn_codes()
examples <- examples[examples$pcode %in% c(
  "MN", "MNR1", "MN84", "MN8401", "MN11", "MN1107", "MN110751"
), ]
knitr::kable(examples[c("name_en", "pcode", "nso_code", "iso_code")])
name_en pcode nso_code iso_code
Mongolia MN 0 MN
Western region MNR1 1 NA
Ulaanbaatar MN11 511 MN-1
Khovd MN84 184 MN-043
Bayangol MN1107 51107 NA
Jargalant MN8401 18401 NA
1-r khoroo MN110751 5110751 NA

Use mn_codes("aimag") for all aimags and the capital. To see a few khoroos and whether they have a boundary:

knitr::kable(mn_codes("bag", within = "Baganuur")[
  c("name_en", "pcode", "nso_code", "has_geometry")
])
name_en pcode nso_code has_geometry
1-r khoroo MN110151 5110151 TRUE
2-r khoroo MN110153 5110153 TRUE
3-r khoroo MN110155 5110155 TRUE
4-r khoroo MN110157 5110157 TRUE
5-r khoroo MN110159 5110159 TRUE

Rural bags and villages have names and codes, but their boundaries are not included. has_geometry = FALSE identifies these entries. See Bring your own bag boundaries.

Resolve repeated names

Several soums share names such as Bayan-Uul. Restrict the search to the right parent with within.

mn_match("Bayan-Uul", level = "soum", within = "Dornod")
#> [1] "MN2110"
mn_match("Sukhbaatar district", within = "Ulaanbaatar")
#> [1] "MN1119"

Without enough information, mn_match() returns NA and warns about the possible matches. Inspect the candidates before choosing:

matches <- mn_match("Bayan-Uul", level = "soum", details = TRUE)
#> Warning: 1 value matches more than one unit and became "NA":
#> • Bayan-Uul: Bayan-Uul (MN2110, Dornod); Bayan-Uul (MN8207, Govi-Altai)
#> ℹ Use `within` (for example the aimag) to choose one.
matches[c("x", "pcode", "status")]
#> # A tibble: 1 × 3
#>   x         pcode status   
#>   <chr>     <chr> <chr>    
#> 1 Bayan-Uul NA    ambiguous

The warning in this example is intentional. When joining rows from several aimags, use by_parent; see Putting your data on a map.

Check spelling corrections

The matcher ignores case and punctuation and uses words such as “aimag” or “district” to help identify the level. It can also suggest a close spelling. Review these suggestions before using them.

mn_match("Ulanbaatr", details = TRUE)[c("x", "pcode", "status")]
#> # A tibble: 1 × 3
#>   x         pcode status
#>   <chr>     <chr> <chr> 
#> 1 Ulanbaatr MN11  fuzzy

To disallow approximate spelling matches, set fuzzy = FALSE. For a join that must stop on uncertain matches, use mn_join(..., strict = TRUE).

Convert Cyrillic to Latin letters

mn_translit() converts spelling; it does not identify a place or check that it exists.

x <- c("Өвөрхангай", "Сүхбаатар")
mn_translit(x)
#> [1] "Övörkhangai" "Sükhbaatar"
mn_translit(x, to = "nso")
#> [1] "Uvurkhangai" "Sukhbaatar"

The default uses MNS 5217:2012. to = "nso" gives the plain Latin spellings used in NSO English tables.
